## 388e9ae29018

**Reproduced generator-contract defect.** Generator SHA-256
`cff7fbd6a45be9f6f3e60a16f99a5a8a828f17276a0fa073da55a1817f10b536`
accepts `palette_kind="garbage"` even though `AXES` declares the only valid value
as `fixed`. With seed `314159`, sample index `7`, difficulty `medium`, it emitted
a 15×18 input, `self_check` returned no errors, and the selected Racket rule
executed successfully. The source also has no `RULE_HASH` declaration, while the
executed/catalog rule hash is `07d0b4adce4b`.

Exact input, metadata, source hashes, and Racket output are retained in
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/generator_counterexample.json`; the supported apply
record is `checks/audit/388e9ae29018/racket.json`. This demonstrates that an
out-of-domain advertised override can silently enter the accepted training
stream. The audit target was not modified.

audits.text:
## 388e9ae29018

Audited generator SHA-256:
`cff7fbd6a45be9f6f3e60a16f99a5a8a828f17276a0fa073da55a1817f10b536`.
Selected and executed canonical rule hash: `07d0b4adce4b`.
The same-source prior return `review-baa9b009b81b43b3:v0001` was read as a
lead. Its invalid `palette_kind` finding was not rerun and is not claimed as
a new measurement here.

### Reproduced defects

**The generated and validated domain excludes the canonical task's object
roles.** The canonical rule handles red shrinkers and gray growers that can
be diamonds or V shapes, and preserves unrelated colored objects. In
contrast, every generator branch paints only colors `{2,5,7}`, with the
ordinary branch restricted to complete diamond outlines. All four unique
canonical inputs were rejected by `self_check` and by public apply's
generator-domain diagnostic, despite all four canonical outputs matching
actual Racket execution.

Canonical inputs are 16×16 with four or five colors. Every generated input
has at most three colors, so the canonical color-count envelope is
unreachable. A focused sample at seed `71731`, indices `0..19` per band,
confirmed **0/20 exact and 0/20 envelope hits in each of easy, medium and
hard**. For example, canonical train pair 0 is rejected for colors 8 and 9,
absence of a complete gray diamond, and four gray cells outside complete
outlines. These are canonical features, not malformed author inputs.

**A valid exact-size request is silently enlarged when placement is
incompatible.** With seed `0`, sample index `0`, difficulty `easy`, and
`grid_h=12, grid_w=12, texture="r3", gray_radius=2`, the generator returns
an **18×18** grid containing a red radius-3 diamond and a gray radius-2
diamond. Its self-check returns `[]`, and public apply accepts and executes it.
The requested height and width are valid easy-band values. For the sampled
radii, both centers must lie in coordinates `4..7`; their maximum Manhattan
separation is 6, while placement requires at least `3+2+3=8`. The fallback
enlarges the grid after retries instead of rejecting the incompatible exact
request. A repair should preserve the request or explicitly reject that joint
combination.

**The named radius controls are independently ignored.** With sample index
`0`, difficulty `easy`, and `red_radius="r3", gray_radius=2`:

| Seed | Requested radius | Observed radius |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | red 3 | red 2 |
| 2 | gray 2 | gray 1 |

Both generated inputs pass self-check and produce valid Racket outputs.
These cases distinguish the named `red_radius` control from the supported
`texture="r3"` alias; the declared names should not silently behave differently.

### Suspected shortcut and domain-transfer risk

A solver that discards colors outside `{2,5,7}` cannot be distinguished from
the intended preservation behavior on this generator's outputs, because such
colors never occur. The runnable comparison removes those colors from the
correct Racket output: it differs on each of the four canonical pairs while
agreeing trivially on the generated witnesses. The code's absence of V
shapes likewise leaves the canonical V behavior untaught.

This is a source-supported domain-transfer risk, **not** a reproduced
ambiguous production lesson: there is no generated query with an unrelated
color or V shape against which to demonstrate such a lesson failure. No
solver performance or universal identifiability claim is made.

### Evidence and reproduction

The runnable probe is `checks/audit/388e9ae29018/probe.py`. Exact override
inputs/outputs and a compact canonical witness are in
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/witnesses.json`. Actual Racket results for all
four canonical pairs and all three override witnesses are in
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/racket.json`. Canonical rejection reasons, bounded
profile rows, the joint-constraint explanation and rival differences are in
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/report.json`. Source snapshots are
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/source_generator.py` and
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/canonical_rule.rkt`.

Command, cwd, actual exit code, probe hash and elapsed time are in
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/run_receipt.json`, with logs in
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/stdout.txt` and
`checks/audit/388e9ae29018/stderr.txt`.

From the packet root `/workspace/scratch/99b24ae817e4/arc_review`:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 WORK/.venv/bin/python review.py run ../.venv/bin/python ../checks/audit/388e9ae29018/probe.py
```

The payload runs from `WORK/repo`. Observed exit code: **0**. Seven retained
inputs were executed by Racket. The additional 60 profile draws were
input-only diagnostics.
